changelog:
# JediCoop patch notes

## 0.16.0
**The world**
- The roots you cut through with your lightsaber on Kashyyyk are cut for both of you, so you can both get past them.
- When your friend swings on a rope, the rope swings with them on your screen instead of hanging still beside them.

**Fights**
- An enemy no longer dies on your screen while it's still alive for your friend.

**Story together**
- Music is no longer held back while you wait for each other: it changes for each of you as you play.

**Smoother play**
- Fixed small hitches every few seconds while playing together.
- Both players need JediCoop 0.16.0.

## 0.15.3
**Story together**
- Story moments now wait for both of you. When one of you reaches a story trigger or a cutscene first, you see
  "Waiting for <your friend>", and it plays for both of you together once they get there.

**Fixes**
- Fixed bounty hunters (and other enemies) sometimes appearing twice for the joining player, with the extra ones
  only on their screen.
- A boss's health bar now stays on screen for both of you for the whole fight, and shows the boss's name in capitals
  like the game's own.
- Both players need JediCoop 0.15.3.

## 0.15.2
- Rocket and grenade blasts now make their explosion sound for both of you, not only for the player they were fired at.
- Your friend's double-bladed lightsaber no longer loses its hilt when they're further away.
- Works with friends on 0.15.0 and 0.15.1.

## 0.15.1
- When your friend meditates, they stay at the meditation spot on your screen instead of disappearing.
- When you both meditate at the same time, your friend's BD-1 no longer floats in your meditation screen.
- Works with friends still on 0.15.0.

## 0.15.0
**No pause in co-op**
- While you play together, opening the menu no longer pauses the game for both of you. Your friend keeps playing,
  and sees that you're in the menu or meditating.

**Fights**
- An enemy you're both fighting stays where it is instead of switching between you.

**Cutscenes**
- Your friend no longer shows up standing in the middle of your cutscenes.

**Join Journey**
- The PLAYERS tile shows 2 of 2 once you're connected to the host.
- Both players need JediCoop 0.15.0.

## 0.14.0
**Fights**
- Unblockable attacks aimed at your friend now glow orange on your screen. Red still means it's coming for you.
- When your friend hits an enemy, you see its health bar too, and a boss's health bar shows for both of you.
- Bounty hunters have the same names for both of you, the same one carries the big health bar, and the
  "defeated" banner names the same hunter.
- An enemy you're both hitting no longer keeps switching between you.

**Enemies that appear near one of you**
- The Chompers that pop out of holes on Zeffo now appear for both of you, even if only one of you went near the hole.
- The spiders that jump out of web traps on Kashyyyk now appear for both of you when one of you steps on the web.

**The world**
- When one of you rides or calls an elevator, it moves in both games, so nobody is left behind or seen floating.
- A bridge one of you Force pushes down is down for both of you.
- Zeffo's spinning gears turn in step in both games, also while one of you slows them.
- Your friend's BD-1 glows like yours.
- At a workbench, your friend no longer stands inside you or puts their lightsaber over yours.
- Both players need JediCoop 0.14.0.

## 0.13.0
**Enemies look the same on both screens**
- An enemy's effects now show where they really are: muzzle flashes and shots leave the barrel, flames come out of
  the flamethrower, and the red glint of an unblockable attack sits on the enemy.
- The Purge trooper's shock grenade, its lightning field and its charged shot show for both of you.
- Grenade and rocket blasts show for both of you.
- Enemy shields and cloth look the same in both games.

**Your friend**
- You can hear your friend: their footsteps, their lightsaber and BD-1.
- Your friend's lightsaber lights up the room around it, in their blade colour.
- Blocks, parries and hits on your friend throw sparks on your screen too.

**Encounters**
- Groups of enemies that appear by themselves as you come near now appear for both of you.
- Both players need JediCoop 0.13.0.

## 0.12.0
**Enemies in co-op**
- Enemies move the same way on both screens. When an enemy switches from fighting one of you to the other, it no
  longer jumps across the room: it carries on from where it was.
- Enemies near you move more smoothly, and keep up better on a slower connection.
- Blaster bolts are real on both screens: a bolt fired at your friend flies, hits and can be blocked or parried
  where you see it.
- Both players need JediCoop 0.12.0.

## 0.11.0
**Closed testing**
- Until the public release, co-op is for approved players: sign in with Discord in the launcher, and type /apply in the
  Jedi Co-op Discord if you're not approved yet. If you're not signed in or approved, the game tells you what to do
  instead of failing to connect.
- Both players need JediCoop 0.11.0.

**Discord**
- Your Discord profile now shows what you're doing in Jedi Co-op: in the menus, playing solo, hosting a co-op
  journey or playing with a friend, with how far through the story the journey is and how long you've been playing.
- While you host a co-op journey with a free seat, friends can press Ask to Join on your profile. When you accept in
  Discord, their game opens Join Journey with your code already filled in, and they press Join. If their game isn't
  running, the launcher starts it for them (launcher 1.3.0).
- Your join code is never shown on your profile.
- Don't want it? Set Presence=0 under [Discord] in JediCoop.ini.

## 0.10.2
- Fixed in-game messages showing as a plain text box at the top of the screen on some planets (for
  example at the start of the game on Bracca), instead of the game's own style.
- Fixed a crash for the joining player a few seconds after resuming a co-op journey.
- The line under your friend's name no longer flickers.
- "Partner joined" and the other centre messages now play their whole animation, and short messages stay a
  little longer.
- The host no longer gets the join-code message after resuming a journey their friend has already joined.
- Join Journey: the journeys under YOUR JOURNEYS can be clicked again, and the keyboard and controller now move
  between all of them, not just the first.
- Join Journey: Esc (or B) now goes back one step, to Online Co-op, instead of back to the title menu with the code
  boxes left on screen.
- Join Journey: rejoining a journey, PLAYERS now shows 2 of 2 once you're connected to the host (it always said 1 of 2).

## 0.10.1
**In-game messages**
- In-game messages now look like the game's own notifications and banners: your friend joining or
  leaving, meditating or flying off, finds you share, and anything that goes wrong when joining.
- "Follow?" can be answered on a controller too: D-pad right to follow, left to stay.

**Seeing your friend**
- Your friend's name shows above their head, with how far away they are, and an arrow at the edge of
  the screen points the way when they're out of view.
- On the holomap your friend has an arrow of their own. When you're on different planets, the map
  says where they are.

**Co-op in the pause menu**
- Co-op now has its own CO-OP tab in the pause menu, after SETTINGS. Host a game, join one with a
  code, see who you're playing with and leave the session there. F4, F6, F7 and F8 are no longer
  used.
- A clipboard button next to the code boxes (on the CO-OP tab and in Join Journey) pastes a join code
  you've copied.
- Codes can be entered with a controller: up and down change the letter, left and right move.
- Your recovery code is on the CO-OP tab, hidden until you hold R (Y on a controller).

**Good to know**
- A friend still on JediCoop 0.10.0 can play with you; each of you sees the new look once you've updated.
- If a message ever looks wrong on your screen, set Style=Classic under [Overlay] in JediCoop.ini
  (next to the game's exe) for plain text messages instead.

## 0.10.0
**Co-op journeys**
- A new Online Co-op entry on the game's title screen. Host a co-op journey of your own and play it
  with a friend whenever you both have time; it carries on where you left off.
- Start a new co-op journey: pick the difficulty, choose the co-op settings, then begin the journey.
  Your friend can join once it first saves after the opening.
- Join Journey: type your friend's code (or use the one you copied) and you're taken into their game.
  The first time, you start with the host's Cal; after that you keep your own Cal, outfit, skills and
  finds every time you come back.
- Your journeys are listed with the planet you're on, who you play with and when you last played
  together. Delete a journey, or export it to one of your own save slots.

**Co-op settings, per journey**
- Enemy health: Normal, Tougher or Toughest. The host's choice applies to both players.
- Unlocks: Your own (each player keeps what they find) or Shared (stims, essences and chests found
  by one player count for both, and are gone from the other player's world, so nothing can be picked
  up twice). With Shared, anything found while you were away is waiting when you return.

**Recovery code**
- The launcher and the co-op menu (F4) show your recovery code. Enter it in the launcher on another
  PC to keep your progress in your friends' journeys. Keep it to yourself.

**Good to know**
- Both players need JediCoop 0.10.0 to play together. The launcher updates itself to 1.2.0 first,
  then offers JediCoop 0.10.0.
- Co-op journeys never touch your own save slots unless you export one there.

## 0.9.9
**Co-op fixes**
- The joining player no longer sees "Shortcut unlocked" for shortcuts the host had opened earlier.
- You can see the Purge troopers' shots aimed at your friend, and their shots at you hurt and can be
  parried. Rocket troopers' missiles show up too.
- Heavy gunners raise their shield in both games.
- Fixed an invisible obstacle where an enemy your friend had already defeated used to stand.
- Fixed co-op sometimes stopping for the rest of the session after the host respawned or rode a lift.
- Blocking blaster shots aimed at you now sends them back at the trooper, even when the trooper is
  being controlled from your friend's game.
- Enemies now go after whichever of you is nearer, and turn on a player their shots hit, without
  breaking off an attack halfway.
- Troopers' blasters no longer float away from their hands, and those troopers no longer jitter.
- Flametroopers' flames, baton trails and other attack effects now show in both games.
- AT-ST shots now show up for both players.
- Bounty hunters' laser sights point at the right player, and their wrist rockets explode in both
  games.
- Brute droids and bounty hunters look the same in both games.
- Defeated enemies are much less likely to go flying across the area.
- Fixed an enemy sometimes being missing in one game after a respawn.

## 0.9.8
**Co-op fixes**
- Fixed a crash when some enemies came into view, such as Purge troopers.
- Fixed a rare problem where co-op stopped working for the host while riding a lift into a new area.

## 0.9.7
**Co-op fixes**
- Shortcuts the host has opened are open for the joining player too, including ones opened in an
  earlier session.
- When your friend closes the game, you're told they left, instead of "disconnected".

## 0.9.6
**Co-op fixes**
- Force Slow on puzzle objects looks the same in both games.
- Closing the game ends the co-op session straight away, so your friend isn't left waiting.

## 0.9.5
**Choose the rules before you play**
- New Co-op settings in the launcher, next to Play: the difficulty, following your friend to another
  planet, and the size of JediCoop's messages. Choose them before you start the game; in the game
  you just host (F6) or join (F7).
- Difficulty: Normal (the game as it is), Tougher (enemies have 1.5× health) or Toughest (2×). The
  host's choice is used for both players, so you no longer have to pick the same.
- Following: Ask me (Y / N), Always follow, or Stay.
- The co-op menu (F4) shows the difficulty in use and whose choice it is.
- Both players need 0.9.5 to play together.

**Fixes**
- With Tougher or Toughest, enemies no longer get even tougher each time a player leaves and joins
  again.

## 0.9.4
**Install, Update and Play are separate buttons**
- Install (or Update) and Play are now two buttons. Install or update first and watch each step; then
  Play starts the game.
- While an update is waiting, Play says why: both players need the same version of JediCoop.
- The message under the buttons is easier to read over the background.

## 0.9.3
**See what Install and Update do**
- Install & Play and Update & Play now show each step on the button as it happens: checking the
  game, copying JediCoop's files (with their names and sizes), your settings, checking the installed
  files, and starting the game.
- If a step fails, the launcher shows which one and why, and the button offers Try again.

## 0.9.2
**A new look for the launcher**
- A new design and a new logo, with scenes from the games behind each page.
- What's new is now a page with the notes for every version. It still opens by itself after an
  update.
- Jedi: Survivor has its own page. It shows whether the game is on your PC; co-op for it comes later.
- The game folder, Uninstall and the server address are under Settings.
- Messages appear at the top of the window and never cover a button; click ✕ to dismiss one.

**Tidier install**
- The settings file now holds only the settings you might change: your name, the server, the
  difficulty and the message size. Everything else uses built-in defaults.
- The log file is shorter and easier to send when asking for help.

## 0.9.1
**Updates without reinstalling**
- The launcher now updates itself: when a new version is out, it offers "Update now", installs it in a
  few seconds and restarts. Your settings and saves stay as they are.

**Fixes**
- Joining by code over the internet could fail at once with "Can't reach the JediCoop server".
- A failed join is now shown once instead of twice.
- Save backups are named with your local time, and the launcher says which folder it made.
- Launcher messages no longer cover the buttons.

## 0.9.0
The first version with the JediCoop launcher and join codes.

**Getting started**
- The JediCoop launcher finds your game (Steam or EA app), checks it's a supported version, and
  installs, updates or removes the mod with one click. It never changes the game's own files.
- Set your name once in the launcher; press Play to start the game with JediCoop.
- Back up your saves, or import a save a friend sent you, from the launcher.

**Play together**
- Host: press F6 in the game. You get a join code (like K7Q-X9R), already copied: paste it to your
  friend. No extra software or router settings needed.
- Join: copy the code, then press F7 in the game (or press F7 and type it).
- See your friend's Cal in your game, with lightsaber, poncho and BD-1.
- Fight together: shared enemies, damage and deaths in both games; blaster bolts, acid spit and
  baton strikes from enemies the other game runs hit you too, with the game's own knockback and
  sparks. Block bolts to stop them.
- Travel separately: each player flies their own Mantis. When one picks a planet, the other is
  asked "Follow? [Y] / [N]".
- Shared world: a shortcut door unlocked by one player opens for both; Force Slow on a puzzle
  object slows it in both games.
- Difficulty: Co-op (the normal game) or Scaled (tougher enemies for two players).

**Menus and messages**
- F4 opens the co-op menu (session, join code, keys, your name, difficulty, mod version).
- Join problems are explained: a wrong code, or a different mod or game version, says so plainly.

**Safety**
- Back up your saves from the launcher before playing together (one click, dated copies).

**Known limits**
- Force Slow on an object looks different in the other player's game.
- Parrying a bolt back only works for bolts aimed at you.
- Enemies alerted far from one player may stand still in that player's game until they're defeated.
- Some enemy types and bosses are untested.
